paragraphs: (Hyman explains the Greek epithet as “preacher.”) The supplied text mentions Berakhot and then cites Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 1, on “For better,” section 2, where Rabbi Chanina son of Rabbi Acha speaks in his name.

notes.text: The supplied ברכות stands without a locator before the Shir HaShirim Rabbah citation and is retained as a separate reference. Its attachment and occurrence remain unverified. “Preacher” is Hyman’s explanation of the Greek epithet, not an independently established etymology here.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1240) cites Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:2 and Tanchuma, Beshalach, note 91. Berakhot names Rabbi Tanchum bar Iskolastika and gives his prayer. Guggenheimer renders the epithet “the scholar.” In Beshalach §17, note 91, Buber explains a related plural in the story of Shapur’s advisers as Greek scholastikos, a learned person devoted to study. Hyman’s print places the Song of Songs Rabbah citation under the next heading, Tanchum bar Acha. In that midrash, Chanina son of Rabbi Ada speaks in the name of Tanchum bar Acha. The supplied text combines the two notices and gives Chanina’s father as Acha.
